newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: STIC in phone network investment.
newsitem.headline: STIC in phone network investment.

text.p: Singapore Technologies Telemedia Pte Ltd (STT) said on Wednesday its joint venture with Malaysian firm Sapura Telecoms was investing Singapore $30 million over five years in a new telecoms project.
STT officials told a news conference the unit, ST Advanced Radio, would operate a radio-based digital mobile telecommunications network in Singapore, called MobiTalk.
They said MobiTalk network was expected to take 50 percent of Singapore's business mobile communications market and be profitable inside two years.
ST Advanced Radio is 80 percent owned by STT and 20 percent by Sapura. STT is part of the same group as Singapore Technologies Industrial Corp (STIC).
U.S. electronics company Motorola would supply the technology for the new network, the officials said.
ST Advanced Radio's general manager Philip Tan said there could be as many as 50,000 business mobile communications users Singapore-wide by 2000.

If the new system was successful in Singapore, the partners might expand into other Asian territories, he said. The two companies had already made a joint investment in a small wireless company in the Philippines, he said.
